newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai SEC seeks high quality firms for listing.
newsitem.headline: Thai SEC seeks high quality firms for listing.

text.p: Thai Securities and Exchange Commission chief Pakorn Malakul Na Ayudhya said on Thursday he would try to persuade more companies with strong fundamentals to list on the local bourse from next year.

"The SEC also plans to propose a cut in corporate tax for all listed companies on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. This will be aimed at encouraging good companies to list on the exchange," said Pakorn.

He was speaking at a news conference to outline the regulatory body's plans and proposals for 1997. The SEC will also seek cooperation from financial institutions to pursuade more joint ventures between Thai and foreign investors to be listed on the bourse, he said.
"This will add to the number of shares with strong fundamentals in the market," he said.

The SEC also planned to grant foreign exchange licences to securities companies next year to increase business for those companies, he said. Thai securities companies currently are not allowed to do foreign exchange business.
The agency would also approve new mutual fund licenses to raise the number of local institutional investors from the current 15 companies, he added.
